chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Humayd ibn Ziyad, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from more than one, from Aban, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Regarding a man who marries a woman and finds in her a defect, which is blindness, or whiteness (of skin), or leprosy, he has the right to return (divorce) her, provided he has not yet consummated the marriage.

key_terms.بَيَاضًا: whiteness (specifically albinism or pale skin condition)
key_terms.يَدْخُلْ بِهَا: he enters with her (consummates the marriage)
key_terms.يَرُدُّهَا: he returns her (annuls the marriage/divorces her without full dower)

ai.seo_question: What are the valid reasons for a husband to return his wife before consummation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the legal mechanism of *Tadlis* (concealment of defects) in Shia jurisprudence, granting the husband the right to annul the marriage if specific physical impairments—blindness, albinism, or leprosy—are discovered before consummation. It highlights the principle that these conditions, while not necessarily invalidating the contract, constitute grounds for rescission due to their impact on marital life, distinguishing them from defects that do not warrant return.
